name: hmmer
desc: Build profile HMMs and scan against sequence databases
why: Profile hidden Markov models scanning sequence databases is real bioinformatics you can run at home on protein families.

brief.what_it_is: HMMER is a suite of command-line tools for biosequence analysis using profile hidden Markov models (profile HMMs). You can build a profile from your own multiple sequence alignment with hmmbuild, then search sequence databases with hmmsearch. You can scan a sequence against a curated profile database such as Pfam with hmmscan. You can also start from a query sequence instead of a profile, as BLAST does, using phmmer or the iterative jackhmmer. The package's executable list also includes nhmmer and nhmmscan for DNA, plus alignment, conversion, and database tools. Inputs are sequence files and profile or alignment files, and outputs are search hits and alignments.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage says HMMER is for searching sequence databases for homologs and for making sequence alignments, and it is built to detect remote homologs as sensitively as possible. It frames profile HMMs as the way to do this, noting that they were first introduced at significant computational expense, but that as of HMMER3 it is essentially as fast as BLAST.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage describes the method only at a high level: it uses probabilistic models called profile HMMs, built from conserved protein domains or DNA elements or from a multiple sequence alignment, and it relies on the strength of those underlying probability models for sensitivity. It does not explain the internal algorithm further. The user guide PDF was linked but could not be read as text.
brief.install_notes: The homepage offers the latest version v3.4 as a source download, plus precompiled packages and archived older versions. No build requirements, dependencies, or first-run steps appear on the homepage. The user guide, which would likely cover these, could not be read.
brief.standout: Profile HMMs give HMMER good sensitivity for remote homologs that plain pairwise search can miss, and HMMER3 claims that this is now about as fast as BLAST. It is a whole toolkit of about nineteen executables covering build, search, scan, alignment, and database preparation, not a single tool.
brief.status: Maintained, as far as the homepage shows: it lists v3.4 as the latest version, and it links a blog about HMMER3 and an EBI-hosted search server. No release date or last-commit date was visible, so the exact activity level is unknown.
brief.caveats: The homepage says nothing about license, supported platforms, or build difficulty. The user guide PDF came back as raw compressed bytes, so I could not confirm any of those details or the exact command syntax. Most of the value depends on having profile databases such as Pfam available, which the homepage presents as a common pairing but does not supply. The brew description and scout notes say you can run it at home on protein families, which the homepage supports only in general terms.
quotes: HMMER is designed to detect remote homologs as sensitively as possible, relying on the strength of its underlying probability models.
as of HMMER3, HMMER is essentially as fast as BLAST.
HMMER can also start with your query sequences, not just profiles, just like BLAST.
fetch_log: http://hmmer.org/ - worked, returned the homepage text with the v3.4 release note, the tool descriptions, and links.
http://eddylab.org/software/hmmer/Userguide.pdf - returned raw compressed PDF stream data with no readable text, so it gave no usable commands or install details.
